title: School-based HPV vaccination campaign in a French region during the 2024-2025 school year: Incentives deployed and analysis of parental consent return.
content: To describe parental consent return for HPV vaccination among seventh-grade students (ages 12-13) in the French region of Nouvelle-Aquitaine during the 2024-2025 school vaccination campaign. In September 2024, 12,023 consents were obtained, representing a decrease compared with the previous school year. To address this decline, the digital consent platform was reopened between January 20 and March 10, 2025, supported by weekly monitoring using a three-color indicator and regular coordination with the three regional education authorities and the Regional Health Agency. During this reopening period, 1506 additional consents were collected. In parallel, a communication strategy based on social marketing was deployed. By the end of the school year, 13,714 consents had been obtained, leading to the vaccination of 10,607 seventh-grade students. These measures partially offset the initial decline in consents and suggest that real-time monitoring with tailored communication can improve campaign effectiveness.

title: Buffalo Puppet Procession Traces Native History Through NYC’s Streets
content:
Buffalo Puppet Procession Traces Native History Through NYC’s Streets
“Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi” pays homage to 38 Dakota men executed by President Abraham Lincoln in Mankato, Minnesota, in 1862.
A herd of 40 life-sized buffalo puppets migrated through Lower Manhattan today, September 18, plodding through Bowling Green, Federal Hall, the World Trade Center, Chinatown, and several other historical sites along their trail. On the second and final leg of its procession, Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi (Lakota for "buffalo trail home") will also hit downtown Brooklyn tomorrow, September 19.
Theater writer and director Amir Nizar Zuabi created the project with descendants of the Lenape, the original Indigenous inhabitants of New York, and Lakota elders, whose deeply sacred relationship with the mammal dates back thousands of years.
“We just followed the elders’ lead in who they wanted involved, what they wanted to be said, really letting them shape the conceptual backbone of the work,” JJ Lind (Cherokee-Shawnee), the artistic director for the performance group Immediate Medium, told Hyperallergic.
“We’d bring community members in to provide feedback on the activities that happen along the route,” he added.
At nine historic sites throughout Manhattan, such as Broad Street Plaza and Zuccotti Park, concurrent performances from the Native dance troupes, gospel choirs, and Lenape youth created a lively backdrop. From the rampant slaughter of buffalo in the 19th century to the species' recovery led by Native activists and conservationists, the procession traces the buffalo’s complex history in the United States.

title: Social Design Award 2026 »Wir schaffen Verbindungen!«: Wählen Sie Ihren Favoriten!
content:
Social Design Award 2026 Wählen Sie Ihren Lieblingshelfer!
Wenn die Gesellschaft sich polarisiert, wird sie schwächer. Und ungerechter. Und härter. Deshalb wurden beim diesjährigen Social Design unter dem Motto »Wir schaffen Verbindungen« Projekte gesucht, die das Miteinander stärken.
In Kooperation mit
Rund 300 Einsendungen gab es, von größeren Initiativen und einzelnen Engagierten oder von Social-Design-Büros und gemeinnützigen Unternehmen. Die Jury hat sie gesichtet und aus diesen die besten zehn ausgesucht. Und nun sind Sie dran: Wählen Sie aus dieser Shortlist Ihr Lieblingsprojekt, das den mit 2500 Euro dotierten Publikumspreis gewinnen soll.
100% WIR – Die Haustür-Initiative
100% WIR
Demokratie lebt davon, dass alle mitmachen, miteinander diskutieren und: wählen. In dem südniedersächsischen Ort Heckenbeck (Bad Gandersheim) entwickelten deshalb Marlene Brandt, Manfred Mudelsee, und Tobias Polzin ihr Pilotprojekt »100% Heckenbeck«. Vor der Bundestagswahl 2025 suchten 3 Prozent der Heckenbecker 97 Prozent der Haushalte in Zweierteams auf und sprachen mit diesen – über das Wahlsystem, über aktuelle Politik, über Demokratie und wie wichtig es ist, dass alle ihre Kreuze setzen bei der Bundestagswahl.
In den USA sind solche Haustürgespräche üblich, in Deutschland machen dies nur wenige Parteien. In Heckenbeck kamen Ehrenamtliche ins Gespräch mit politisch Interessierten und Nichtwählern, mit Anhängern verschiedenster Parteien, mit alten Menschen, die Schwierigkeiten hatten, zum Wahllokal zu gelangen. Dabei vermittelten die Ehrenamtlichen keine parteipolitischen Positionen, denn die Initiative ist überparteilich. Sie hatten zum Ziel, die Demokratie zu stärken, Polarisierungen zu überwinden und in einen nachbarschaftlichen Austausch zu kommen.
Und weil es nebenbei auch darum ging, Menschen aus ihrer sozialen Isolation zu holen, schloss sich an die Besuche ein Begegnungs-Café an, bei dem weiterdiskutiert werden konnte.
ApplicAid
ApplicAid e.V.
Foto: ApplicAid e.V.Stipendien sollen Talente fördern und Türen öffnen. Doch die Ungleichheit zeigt sich bereits dort, wo über Chancen entschieden wird: bei der Vergabe. Das möchte ApplicAid ändern. Der Verein bringt Stipendiat:innen mit jungen Menschen zusammen, die trotz Talent und Leistungsbereitschaft auf strukturelle Hürden stoßen: etwa als Erstakademiker:innen, Menschen mit Migrationsgeschichte, mit niedrigem sozioökonomischem Status oder chronischen Erkrankungen.
Was ihnen auf dem Weg zum Stipendium fehlt, ist selten die Qualifikation, sondern der Zugang zum richtigen Netzwerk. Seit 2020 schließt ApplicAid diese Lücke durch individuelle Einzelbetreuung. Je nach Fachrichtung, Stipendium und Hintergrund bringt die Initiative Mentor:in und Mentee zusammen. Sechs Wochen feilen sie per Videochat am Motivationsschreiben, der Selbstdarstellung und dem Auswahlgespräch.
ApplicAid ist kostenlos und deutschlandweit aktiv. Mehr als 1200 Bewerbungen wurden bereits begleitet, 42 Prozent davon waren erfolgreich. Viele erfolgreiche Bewerber:innen werden später selbst Mentor:innen. Sie geben weiter, was ihnen geholfen hat – und halten die Tür für die Nächsten offen. Hinter ApplicAid steht ein Verein, der bereits vom EU-Parlament ausgezeichnet wurde und von verschiedenen Stiftungen finanziell unterstützt wird.
Die Unterhausdebatte
Sind Sie dafür oder dagegen? Was wie Spaltung und Polarisierung klingt, ist der Beginn von Verständnis. Das jedenfalls ist das Konzept der Unterhausdebatte. Bei Veranstaltungen in Bibliotheken, Museen, Konferenzen oder auch auf Marktplätzen stehen die Ja-Stuhlreihen den Nein-Stuhlreihen gegenüber, genau wir im britischen Unterhaus, wo Regierung und Opposition sich gegenübersitzen (und nicht im Halbkreis platziert sind, wie im Deutschen Bundestag). und dann geht die Diskussion los. Und zwar über ein kontroverses Zukunftsthema wie ein Social-Media-Verbot für Kinder, Meinungsfreiheit oder Partei-Verbotsverfahren. Das Moderatorenteam stellt dazu immer wieder einfache Fragen, und das Publikum platziert sich immer wieder neu auf Ja- oder Nein-Stühle. Und dann beginnt die Diskussion. Mit Lösungsbeispiel oder überraschenden Fragen bringt das Moderatorenteam Lebendigkeit in die Diskussion.
Entwickelt wurde das Konzept von den Zukunftsreportern, wie Carina Frey, Rainer Kurlemann, Alexander Mäder sich nennen. Sie gehören zur Genossenschaft RIFFReporter. In Dutzenden von Veranstaltungen haben sie beobachtet, dass die Menschen tiefer ins Nachdenken kommen, wenn sie sich für eine Position entscheiden und diese dann im gemeinsamen Gespräch erläutern. Die anfängliche Polarisierung, so die Erfahrung der RIFFReporter, verhärtet nicht die Fronten, sondern führt im Gegenteil zu mehr Verständnis. In Erinnerung bleiben die Debatten und Argumente dann auch.
Künftig möchten die Zukunftsreporter ermöglichen, dass die Diskussionen weiterlaufen und die Teilnehmer der Debatte sich miteinander vernetzen, digital per App auf dem Handy.
Kulturklüngel
In Köln gibt es eine Reise-Agentur etwas anderer Art. Mit »Kulturklüngel« kann man in andere Kulturen eintauchen, ganz ohne einen Flieger zu besteigen oder auch nur die eigene Stadt zu verlassen. Zum Beispiel bei der »kulinarischen Weltreise in Köln-Kalk«, wo man auf wenigen Metern georgische, äthiopische und kamerunische Küchen findet, dazu syrische oder polnische Supermärkte.
Menschen aus mehr als 180 Nationen leben in Köln. Die verschiedenen Kulturklüngel-Exkursionen führen zu Künstlern, Autoren, Händlern und Gastronomen. Zu Sprachschulen, Musikschulen, Kulturinstituten, Religionsgemeinschaften, Coworking-Spaces mit kulturellem Fokus. Meist zu Fuß. Manchmal auch mit dem Fahrrad. So lernen die Rundgänger jene kennen, an denen sie sonst vielleicht nur vorbeigehen.
Dem Gründer Thomas Bönig geht es bei seinen Führungen auch darum, Vorurteile abzubauen und die positiven, bereichernden Seiten offener und multikultureller Gesellschaften zu zeigen. Hauptsächlich, so berichtet er, werden die Führungen, die 30 bis 45 Euro kosten, von Kölnern genutzt, die ihre Stadt neu kennenlernen möchten. Aber auch die Polizeischule hat die Führungen beispielsweise schon als Fortbildung und zur kulturellen Sensibilisierung genutzt.
MentForMigra
Manchmal beginnt wirksame Hilfe mit einer einzigen Person. So war es bei Moubarak, dem ersten Mentee von MentForMigra. Der Grundschüler, der aus Togo nach Düsseldorf gekommen war, fiel 2010 einer Lehrerin auf. Sie wollte sich dafür einsetzen, dass der begabte Junge nach der vierten Klasse auf ein Gymnasium wechseln konnte. Doch woher sollte die nachhaltige Unterstützung kommen, zumal seine Eltern nur wenig Deutsch sprachen?
In vielen Fällen wäre die Geschichte hier zu Ende. Schulische Erfolge sind in Deutschland weiterhin maßgeblich abhängig vom Elternhaus, mehr als in anderen Ländern. Das ist erneut ein bitteres Ergebnis der aktuellen Pisa-Studie. MentForMigra setzt dem seit 2015 etwas entgegen: Die gemeinnützige Düsseldorfer Unternehmergesellschaft bringt ehrenamtliche Mentorinnen und Mentoren mit Kindern und Jugendlichen mit Flucht- oder Migrationsgeschichte zusammen.
Ab der Grundschule begleiten die Freiwilligen ihre Mentees bei wöchentlichen Treffen, verbessern Lesekompetenz, stärken das Deutsch, helfen, schulische und persönliche Ziele zu entwickeln. Das Programm unterstützt auch die Eltern, etwa bei Fragen zum deutschen Bildungssystem, bei Sprachkursen oder bei der beruflichen Orientierung. Es ist ein Austausch auf Augenhöhe, bei dem nicht nur die Kinder, sondern auch ihre Familien verlässliche und niedrigschwellige Ansprechpersonen bekommen. Heute ist MentForMigra neben Düsseldorf auch an weiteren Standorten aktiv, darunter Meerbusch und Köln.
Moubaraks Mentorin begleitete ihn zum Anmeldetermin am Gymnasium. 2019 machte er Abitur und begann danach ein duales Studium.
Plaudertelefon
PLAUDERTELEFON
Einsamkeit kann schmerzen wie eine Wunde. Und ein gutes Gespräch ist so viel mehr als nur ein Pflaster. Das Projekt Plaudertelefon, das die Bürgerstiftung Stuttgart ins Leben gerufen hat, bringt Menschen zusammen, die sich sonst wohl nicht begegnet wären. Einmal die Woche telefonieren die sorgfältig ausgesuchten »Plauderpaare« miteinander, sprechen über das beste Rezept für Käsekuchen, über Kindheitserinnerungen oder einfach über das Leben.
Davon profitieren beide Seiten: Wer körperlich eingeschränkt ist in seiner Mobilität, vielleicht sogar bettlägerig, wer sich nach dem Tod des Partners oder der Partnerin nach Kontakt sehnt, merkt auf einmal: Es gibt jemand, der mir zuhört, der mir gern zuhört. Und wer sich ehrenamtlich engagiert, erfährt, was andere Menschen umtreibt und entdeckt Verbindendes, manchmal über Generationengrenzen hinweg.
Etwa 130 aktive Plauderpartnerschaften gibt es schon im Stuttgarter Stadtgebiet, und es sollen mehr werden. Ein Ritual, das Vorfreude und Verlässlichkeit schafft und etwas entstehen lässt, das wertvoller ist als alles andere: eine Beziehung zu einem anderen Menschen.
PDA-Initiative
Familien mit einem Kind auf dem Autismus-Spektrum, ADHS oder einer anderen neuronalen Besonderheit, erleben oft, dass Kinder nicht mehr in die Kita oder die Schule gehen können. Dass Beruf und das Privatleben leiden und selbst Freund und Verwandte sich abwenden, weil sie die Herausforderungen für die Eltern nicht verstehen.
Durch die PDA Initiative hat sich ein Netzwerk für Familien mit neurodivergenten Kindern und selbst Betroffenen gebildet. Wie sehr diese Gemeinschaft gebraucht wird, zeigen ihre Anfänge: 2022 begann das Projekt mit sieben Eltern, die sich in einer WhatsApp-Gruppe vernetzten. Nicht einmal ein Jahr später waren mehr als 1000 Menschen Teil der Community, heute sind rund 3700 Familien und Einzelpersonen in einer speziell geschaffenen App vernetzt. Diese wurde vom gemeinnützigen Unternehmen Brains in Mind geführt, die Soziologin Annika Tipp und die Designerin Kora Jünger leiten es.
Diese PDA-Plattform bietet geschützte Räume, in denen Erfahrungen geteilt werden, ohne dass man sich einander erklären muss. Experten und Expertinnen ergänzen ihr Fachwissen und nutzen die besprochenen Themen, um fachlich fundierte Impulse zu geben und neue Perspektiven zu eröffnen. Der von der PDA Initiative ermöglicht Austausch und gibt den Mitgliedern das Gefühl von Zugehörigkeit und emotionalem Halt: Hier werden sie mit ihren Anliegen gesehen. Damit vermittelt sie viel mehr als Wissen: »Seit ich in der Community bin«, so eine Person, »fühle ich mich nicht mehr allein mit dem Problem. Das gibt mir ganz viel Energie.«
Popcorn-Privilegien
Privilegien entscheiden von Geburt an über Chancen: Geschlecht, Staatsbürgerschaft, Vermögen, Bildung. Und sie sind ungleich verteilt. Die Popcorn-Privilegien machen diese Ungerechtigkeit sichtbar: Aus den Antworten auf vier Fragen ergibt sich ein Bild der eigenen Privilegien. Wer viele Privilegien hat, erhält wenig Popcorn – wer wenige hat, erhält viel. Dabei entsteht ein kurzes Gespräch: War das Ergebnis überraschend? Wie fühlt es sich an? Hat jemand vielleicht gemogelt?
Genau in diesem Moment liegt die Wirkung des Formats. Wer sich als privilegiert erlebt und trotzdem nur eine leere Tüte bekommt, empfindet das oft als ungerecht. Genau diese Irritation öffnet den Raum für Gespräche über Gerechtigkeit, Benachteiligung und die eigene Position in der Gesellschaft. Popcorn-Privilegien will Menschen, die sich sonst kaum mit sozialer Ungleichheit beschäftigen.
Die Aktion wurde während der Kasseler Museumsnacht 2025 erstmals aufgeführt. Sie soll anregen zum Nachdenken über unterschiedliche Lebensrealitäten. Wer erlebt, dass nicht alle mit denselben Voraussetzungen starten, entwickelt eher Verständnis für andere Perspektiven – und das stärkt den gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt. Entwickelt hat das Format Raamwerk, ein Studio für Kunst, Soziales und Kommerz aus Kassel.
Straßennachlass
Wer auf der Straße lebt, verliert oft mehr als eine Wohnung: Dokumente verschwinden, Angehörige sind nicht erreichbar, und im Notfall weiß niemand, wer zu benachrichtigen ist. Manchmal bleibt eine verstorbene Person sogar namenlos.
Straßennachlass setzt genau dort an. Die Plattform will obdach- und wohnungslosen Menschen einen kostenfreien, geschützten digitalen Ort für ihre Identität geben: wichtige Dokumente, Vorsorgewünsche, Lebensgeschichte und Notfallkontakte. Die Nutzer bestimmen selbst, was sie festhalten und wem sie vertrauen.
Ein NFC-Armband verbindet die digitale Welt mit dem Alltag. Finden Rettungskräfte oder die Polizei eine bewusstlose oder nicht ansprechbare Person, können sie das Armband scannen und die hinterlegte Vertrauensperson erreichen – ohne dass sensible Daten öffentlich sichtbar werden oder eine Ortung stattfindet. So wird aus einer unbekannten Person wieder ein Mensch mit Namen, Beziehungen und Geschichte.
Entwickelt wurde die Idee gemeinsam mit Akteuren der Hamburger Obdachlosenhilfe. Aktuell befindet sich Straßennachlass in der finalen Test- und Entwicklungsphase. Der nächste Schritt soll der schrittweise Rollout über Einrichtungen der Obdachlosenhilfe sein. Denn ein verlorener Wohnraum darf nicht bedeuten, dass auch Identität, Beziehungen und die eigene Geschichte verloren gehen.
U100: Lebenserfahrung zum Anhören
»Alle Lehrerinnen waren ledige Fräuleins«, erinnert sich Ingrid Schlicht. »Keine hat einen Mann gekriegt. Alle waren tot, in Gefangenschaft oder verletzt.« Ingrid wurde 1942 wurde eingeschult, mitten im Zweiten Weltkrieg. Ihre Familie lebte zwischen Kladow und Groß-Glienicke im Südwesten Berlins.
Schlicht ist eine von rund zwei Dutzend hochbetagten Menschen, die im Podcast »U100 – Generation Kladow« über ihr Leben und die Ortsgeschichte berichten: die Ängste, als sowjetische und später britische Truppen ins Dorf einmarschierten. Die Aufregung als ein DDR-Wasserschutzpolizist über die Havel in den Westen flüchtete. Von Gemeinschaft und Freundschaften in Laubenkolonien.
In Kladow leben heute rund 16.000 Einwohner. Vielen Zugezogenen ist die Geschichte ihrer neuen Heimat kaum bekannt. Das Dreierteam aus Oliver Schmidt (Idee, Projektleitung und Interviews), Christian Meyn (Redaktion und Schnitt) und Sven Hasper (Fotografie) will das mit dem Podcast U100 ändern. Die Erzählungen bauen eine Brücke in die Vergangenheit, zu längst Verstorbenen, und bewahrt persönliche Geschichten in Ausstellungen und Veranstaltungen. So will der Podcast Zusammenhalt stiften: Menschen teilen ihre Erinnerungen, andere hören zu – und kommen ins Gespräch. Und tatsächlich: Inzwischen wird das Projekt vom Stadtteilzentrum, von Kirchengemeinde, Schulen und Museen unterstützt, die beispielsweise Kontakte vermitteln oder Räume zur Verfügung stellen.

title: Justiça libera R$ 2,68 bilhões para pagamentos atrasados do INSS; veja quem tem direito
content:
INSS: pagamentos correspondem a valores que deveriam ter sido pagos pelo governo, mas foram negados ou depositados abaixo do devido (Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil)
Repórter
Publicado em 21 de setembro de 2026 às 21h15.
RESUMO | O Conselho da Justiça Federal (CJF) liberou R$ 3,22 bilhões em RPVs para 278.063 pessoas que venceram ações contra o governo federal. Desse total, R$ 2,68 bilhões serão destinados a processos relacionados ao INSS e a benefícios assistenciais. Para receber, é necessário ter uma ação judicial ganha e uma RPV incluída no lote.
O Conselho da Justiça Federal (CJF) liberou R$ 3,22 bilhões em Requisições de Pequeno Valor (RPVs) para pessoas que venceram processos contra órgãos do governo federal. A maior parte dos recursos, R$ 2,68 bilhões, será destinada a ações envolvendo o INSS e benefícios assistenciais.
O lote inclui 278.063 pessoas, distribuídos em 218.651 processos. Estão incluídos casos de revisão de aposentadorias e pensões, além de ações relacionadas a auxílio por incapacidade e outros benefícios.
Os pagamentos correspondem a valores que deveriam ter sido pagos pelo governo, mas foram negados ou depositados abaixo do devido. Mas, atenção: o benefício ter sido negado pelo INSS, por si só, não garante o pagamento. É necessário ter vencido uma ação judicial e ter uma RPV incluída no lote liberado.
O dinheiro não é depositado diretamente na conta bancária habitual do beneficiário. Os Tribunais Regionais Federais (TRFs) recebem os recursos do CJF e fazem os depósitos em contas abertas individualmente no Banco do Brasil ou na Caixa Econômica Federal.
A data em que cada pagamento estará disponível depende do TRF responsável pelo processo.
A consulta pode ser feita nos sistemas da Justiça Federal, com o número do processo ou o CPF, conforme as regras de cada tribunal. Também é possível verificar se houve expedição da RPV ou liberação do pagamento.
Depois que o valor estiver disponível, o beneficiário poderá sacar o dinheiro na agência indicada ou, em determinadas situações, pedir a transferência para uma conta informada pelo advogado.

title: Ukraine brings back 15 people from Russian occupation, including 96-year-old woman
content:
Ukraine brings back 15 people from Russian occupation, including 96-year-old woman
Another 15 Ukrainians have been brought back from territories temporarily occupied by Russia, including a 96-year-old woman from Kherson Oblast, the oldest of those rescued.
Source: Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets on Facebook
Details: A 74-year-old man managed to leave Kakhovka. He had lived under occupation for years because he feared that leaving could harm his son, who was being held captive by Russia. When his son was released in 2025, the father also decided to leave for territory controlled by Ukraine.
However, other problems had emerged by then: his health had deteriorated over the years. He had suffered a severe stroke, which left him partially paralysed, and developed inflammation of the submandibular gland.
He is now being treated by doctors and experts are helping him reinstate his documents, as Ukrainians returning from the occupation often have expired or lost IDs. He will meet his relatives for the first time in years.
A 96-year-old woman left the occupied village of Zaliznyi Port in Kherson Oblast together with her daughter and son-in-law. The family had been living amid attacks, power outages and food shortages.
The elderly woman required constant assistance, while her son-in-law was using an Ilizarov apparatus on his lower limb. Because of this, they could not leave the occupied territory on their own.
The family is now safe, and the grandmother will have the opportunity to see her grandson.
"Everyone who returns has their own reason for waiting for this day. Some will finally be able to embrace their loved ones after years of occupation. Some will be able to see doctors. And some simply want to be safe. For everyone, it means one thing: no longer living in fear," Lubinets added.
Background: A group of 32 Ukrainian children and teenagers was previously brought back from the occupation. Among them was a six-year-old boy who suffered severe psychological trauma after witnessing a drone strike near a children's playground.

title: ADEM program drives equal education access across Indonesia: Ministry
content:
Puslapdik delegate Setyo Utomo said in a written statement received here on Monday that the secondary education affirmation program gives underprivileged children in remote, frontier, and outermost regions the opportunity to obtain a good education.
"Through this secondary education affirmation program, 57 children from the Highland Papua region have completed senior high school in East Java, Central Java, and Bali since 2023-2026. The program continues this year with 100 students studying in West Java, Banten, East Java, and Central Java," he said.
According to him, the 57 students from Highland Papua who received the scholarship were spread across three regions: 26 in East Java, 13 in Central Java, and 18 in Bali.
"We certainly hope that after completing their studies in Java and Bali, their character, discipline, and mindset will improve, so they can become a generation that brings change to the Highland Papua region," he said.
He explained that these 57 children represent extraordinary potential for the Highland Papua region, especially for its eight districts: Jayawijaya, Yahukimo, Nduga, Tolikara, Pegunungan Bintang, Lanny Jaya, Yalimo, and Mamberamo Tengah.
"We really hope these 57 children can serve as an example for other children in Highland Papua, so that they can follow the same path and become the future generation of Highland Papua," he said.
He expressed hope that children given the opportunity to study outside Papua would receive support, especially from their families.
"We hope parents will also give full support to their children who have the opportunity to study outside Papua. They study outside Papua so that their character, personality, spirit, and mindset can change to help develop their full potential," he said.

title: Top court allows bail for specialised medical care
content: The Supreme Court has held that an undertrial prisoner suffering from an ailment requiring specialised treatment and medical supervision unavailable in jail may be granted post-arrest bail on medical grounds, particularly where continued detention could pose a serious risk to his health or life. A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed passed the ruling while allowing two petitions filed by Zeeshan Majeed Bhatti seeking bail on medical grounds, granting him post-arrest bail in both cases. In its detailed judgment, the court observed that medical reports submitted by the Medical Officer of Central Jail, Rawalpindi, showed that the accused was suffering from serious ailments and was not receiving the specialised treatment required at the jail hospital. The accused was suffering from hypertension, diabetes and cardiac problems, besides complaints of chest pain. Cardiologists had recommended specialised medical examination and treatment, the judgment noted. The apex court observed that the ailments suffered by the accused required specialised treatment and continuous medical supervision, which could not be adequately provided by the jail authorities. It held that continued detention without the required specialised treatment could adversely affect the accused's health and could also pose a danger to his life. Referring to its earlier judgments concerning bail on medical grounds, the court held that post-arrest bail could be granted.

title: Three-Day Methadone Bridge Therapy Keeps People in Opioid Treatment, Study Finds
content:
Methadone remains one of the most effective medications available for opioid use disorder, yet in the United States it is locked behind a regulatory architecture that few other medicines must navigate. Federal law restricts methadone treatment for addiction to specially licensed opioid treatment programs, or OTPs, which are scarce in many regions, often maintain long waitlists, and typically limit intake to narrow windows during the business week. For a person in opioid withdrawal who arrives at a clinic on a Friday afternoon, those structural barriers can mean the difference between starting treatment and returning to the illicit drug supply. A new study from researchers at the University of California, San Francisco and the San Francisco Department of Public Health examines whether a legally sanctioned workaround, the so-called three-day methadone rule, can convert a fleeting moment of readiness into durable treatment engagement.
The three-day rule is a provision of federal regulation that permits practitioners who are not affiliated with an OTP to administer methadone to a patient for the purpose of relieving acute withdrawal symptoms while arranging referral to a licensed program. The allowance is capped at three days, and it cannot be renewed within the same month. In practice, it has historically been used sparingly, because clinicians have worried about safety and because the short window seems ill-suited to overcoming the administrative delays that often accompany OTP enrollment. The new research, published in the journal Addiction Science & Clinical Practice, offers a detailed real-world test of the approach as implemented at the San Francisco General Hospital Bridge Clinic, a low-threshold service designed to meet patients where they are.
The study team, led by Sarah Rosenwohl-Mack of UCSF’s Department of Family and Community Medicine, conducted a retrospective case series covering every patient who initiated methadone under the three-day rule at the Bridge Clinic between June 2024 and July 2025. The setting is notable for an unusual piece of geography: the hospital also houses an opioid treatment program in the same building. When that program could not complete an intake, for example because a patient arrived outside scheduled intake hours or the program was at capacity, staff could refer the person down to the Bridge Clinic, where a dose of methadone could be started immediately under the three-day provision. This bidirectional referral pathway became the study’s central variable.
The researchers tracked two primary outcomes. The first was linkage to an OTP within seven days of receiving the initial Bridge Clinic dose, a window that extends beyond the three-day medication allowance and therefore captures whether the bridge actually carried patients to permanent care. The second was retention in OTP treatment at 30 days, a marker of early stability that addiction medicine researchers view as a meaningful predictor of longer-term benefit. Because methadone carries its own risks, particularly when combined with other sedatives, the team also built in a safety monitoring framework that reviewed urine drug screens, emergency department visits, hospitalizations within seven days, and Medical Examiner overdose reports.
The results are striking for a population that conventional systems routinely lose. Among 166 unique patients who received at least one dose of three-day methadone at the Bridge Clinic, 63 percent, or 104 individuals, successfully linked to an opioid treatment program within seven days. Of those who linked, 62 percent, or 64 patients, were still retained in treatment at the 30-day mark. In a field where attrition between first contact and enrollment has long been considered one of the most stubborn leaks in the continuum of care, the finding suggests that a short bridge of medication can hold a substantial fraction of patients long enough for the formal system to catch up with them.
The most consequential finding, however, concerned the direction of the referral. Using multivariable logistic regression to adjust for other factors, the researchers found that patients who arrived at the Bridge Clinic by referral from the co-located OTP had 3.1-fold higher odds of remaining in treatment at 30 days compared with patients who came through other routes. The interpretation is not that the referral itself dispensed a pharmacological benefit, but that the pathway reflects a coordinated system in which the OTP and the Bridge Clinic function as two doors into the same building of care. A patient handed off from the OTP arrives with an established clinical relationship, a documented treatment plan, and a clear route back, whereas a patient walking in cold must navigate enrollment largely on their own after the three-day window closes.
On the safety side, the record was clean in ways that will reassure clinicians who have hesitated to use the three-day rule. The study identified no methadone-related emergency department visits, no hospitalizations, and no deaths within 30 days of receiving methadone at the Bridge Clinic. The urine drug screen review, designed to flag unexpected results such as methadone positivity in patients not prescribed it or the absence of non-prescribed opioids suggesting diversion, surfaced only one notable case: a single patient who, on closer chart review, turned out to have already been enrolled in methadone treatment elsewhere before receiving a dose at the Bridge Clinic. That finding points to a practical quality-control challenge, ensuring that bridge dosing does not duplicate existing treatment, but it does not undermine the overall safety signal.
The technical logic of the intervention deserves attention. Methadone is a long-acting full mu-opioid receptor agonist with a half-life that supports once-daily dosing, which is precisely why it smooths the cycle of withdrawal and craving that drives much of the daily chaos in untreated opioid use disorder. When a patient presents in withdrawal, the clinical task is to provide enough of the medication to relieve symptoms without accumulating toxicity, which is why Bridge Clinic protocols begin with conservative doses and titrate carefully. The three-day rule fits neatly into this pharmacology: three days of supervised dosing is enough to stabilize a patient physiologically and to interrupt the withdrawal-driven urgency that otherwise pushes people back to fentanyl and other illicit opioids, while the referral machinery works in parallel to secure a permanent slot at an OTP.
The San Francisco team acknowledges intellectual debts in the paper, crediting the Faster Paths Emergency Opioid Withdrawal Protocol at Boston Medical Center, whose published approach informed the local protocol. That lineage matters because it illustrates how low-threshold models are spreading through a kind of open-source clinical adaptation, with programs borrowing and refining each other’s protocols rather than waiting for multi-year trials. The study itself was deemed exempt by the UCSF Institutional Review Board and used retrospectively collected anonymized data, a design that trades the rigor of randomization for the realism of observing how an intervention performs inside the ordinary friction of a public hospital.
The implications reach well beyond one clinic. Opioid treatment programs remain the only legal channel for methadone maintenance in the United States, and their geographic maldistribution means that many counties have no OTP at all. The three-day rule cannot substitute for structural reform, but the study demonstrates that when a low-threshold bridge service and a licensed OTP are deliberately networked, the rule becomes a functional handoff mechanism rather than a rarely used legal footnote. The 3.1-fold retention advantage associated with OTP referral suggests that the return on investment lies in building those connections, ensuring that every bridge dose is paired with a warm pathway back into licensed care. For a lethal epidemic that has proven resistant to conventional outreach, the message is deceptively simple: meet people in withdrawal with medication the same day, and engineer the system so that the door they entered stays open behind them.

title: Australia reaches a major milestone in the effort to end AIDS
content:
On June 5, 1981, the United States Centers for Disease Control issued a report on five young men diagnosed with severe pneumonia caused by a yeast-like fungus then called Pneumocystis carinii. The cases were noteworthy because this infection only affected people with severely compromised immune systems. These young men were previously healthy and in the prime of life.
Barely a year later, the disease had a name – acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, or AIDS – and it was spreading like wildfire among gay men in the United States. In 1983, the cause was discovered: a virus that came to be called the human immunodeficiency virus, or HIV, which was transmitted through bodily fluids including blood and breastmilk.
Four decades, 42 million deaths and 91.4 million infections later, the United Nations target to end AIDS as a global public health threat is in sight. Thanks to a massive and sustained global effort in testing, treatment and prevention, a pandemic that has indiscriminately killed people of all genders, sexualities, ages, ethnicities and nationalities could soon be over.
This week, Australia reached an extraordinary milestone on that journey. It joined a small club of nations – including the United Kingdom, Cambodia, Kenya and Nepal – that have achieved the 95-95-95 targets, according to preliminary data presented by UNSW Sydney researchers at the joint Australasian HIV&AIDS and Sexual and Reproductive Health Conference in Melbourne. The goal, which UNAIDS set in 2020, is for 95 per cent of people with HIV to know their HIV status, for 95 per cent of those people to be receiving treatment, and for 95 per cent of those people to have undetectable levels of the virus in their blood. Australia reached those targets four years ahead of schedule.
Australia recorded 753 new HIV infections in 2025 – a 25 per cent decrease since 2016 – which represents a notification rate of just under three people per 100,000. The rate of diagnoses among men who have sex with men declined by 36 per cent over that same period.
Australia is ahead of patchy international progress. The rate of new infections globally continues to decline, but the fight against HIV/AIDS has suffered from the Trump administration’s massive cuts to international aid funding. The US$2.1 billion retrenchment gutted the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief – an organisation that is estimated to have saved 26 million lives through HIV treatment and prevention – and eliminated the US Agency for International Development, which supported a huge range of HIV prevention and treatment programs, particularly in low-income countries. HIV infections are rising in some countries, including Australia’s near neighbour Fiji.
Australia’s progress has been incredible and admirable, but we can’t take our eye off the ball, says Jessica Michaels, deputy chief executive of ASHM, a peak organisation of health professionals. “None of us is under the illusion that we can sit down and put our feet up; I think there’s still an enormous amount of work to do.”
“We can say we’ve achieved things nationally,” says Dr Skye McGregor, an epidemiologist at the Kirby Institute. But, she says, these gains are not experienced equally.
Nearly two thirds of all new HIV cases in Australia in 2025 were gay or bisexual men, more than half of whom were born overseas, with men born in South-East Asia at particularly high risk. By comparison, the number of new infections among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people is small – 37 new cases in 2025 – but it has increased from a low of 16 in 2020, and the diagnosis rate among Indigenous Australians is nearly twice that of non-Indigenous Australians born in this country.
“None of us is under the illusion that we can sit down and put our feet up; I think there’s still an enormous amount of work to do.”
Speaking at the sexual health conference in Melbourne this week, Dawn Casey – chief executive of the National Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisation – said Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health workers and health practitioners were the reason behind the overall success in addressing HIV and other sexually transmitted infections in Indigenous communities.
However, she noted that short funding cycles meant health workers often had to leave communities in which they had built up trust and relationships.
“What treats people is a health worker who knows their family; a health check that opens the conversation before anyone is worried; a test that gives an answer before they leave the room; a medicine that is available; and a relationship that started years before any of it was needed,” she told the conference.
Deaths from AIDS-related illness are extremely rare but not zero, and one third of HIV infections are still being diagnosed late – at least four years after initial infection. A range of barriers to accessing HIV testing means there has always been a persistent group of undiagnosed individuals in Australia, says Scott Harlum, president of the National Association of People with HIV Australia (NAPWHA). “One of the simple [barriers] really is because people’s sexual lives are things that they don’t necessarily want exposed to the world,” he says.
While community designed and led HIV testing programs aimed at gay and bisexual men have been successful in encouraging and normalising HIV testing among men who have sex with men, the highest proportion of late diagnoses – 58 per cent – are in heterosexual men. The second-highest rate of late diagnoses is among South-East Asian-born gay and bisexual men. “A person whose risk of HIV comes about in some way that they don’t want people to know about, they’re not going to walk into a place that’s heavily branded with pride flags, rainbow flags, for example,” Harlum says.
Accessing testing in regional and remote areas can also be challenging, he says. “They’re not going to go into their doctor’s surgery and request a HIV test, because their mother’s friend could be the person on the front desk.”
To address these issues, NAPWHA launched hivtest.au: a website where people can order a HIV self-testing kit. Postcode data from that service suggests many of the kits are going to regional and remote areas, where there may be limited access to sexual health clinics, and also to areas where cultural stigma may be a barrier, such as Western Sydney.
Australia has some of the lowest barriers in the world to accessing prevention, in the form of a daily dose of oral antiretroviral drugs that can be taken to prevent infection, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). As of March, even people who aren’t eligible for Medicare coverage are able to access PrEP. The new long-acting injectable forms that will soon be on the market will offer more choice, although cost and lack of Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme subsidy will likely put them out of the reach of most people.
Similarly, HIV treatment is free or very low cost in Australia, and can also be accessed without Medicare.
Dr James Gray, principal director of the Australia program at Health Equity Matters, the national federation of Australian HIV organisations, says Australia’s partnership approach to HIV prevention and treatment from the very beginning – with leadership from affected communities and their representative organisations – has been pivotal to its success.
“Most of the community-based organisations that are still operating today are over 40 years old now, so they did come together right at the very start of the epidemic,” Gray says. “When you go to community and community-based organisations, you can often identify barriers and challenges that might not be immediately recognisable in other parts of the health system.”
HIV also hasn’t been politicised in Australia in the way it was in other nations, and that bipartisanship has remained solid even as political winds changed direction.
Scott Harlum was a young man when HIV first appeared. “I imagined that one day I might wake up and there’d be a news alert saying, ‘We found a cure, it’s all over,’ ” he says. While a cure is still out of reach, the treatments available are so successful that HIV/AIDS organisations are now contemplating the new challenges of how to help older people with HIV transition into aged care.
“There was a whole demographic of gay men in particular who just were wiped out by AIDS, so to have a population which is now ageing is a wonderful, wonderful thing,” Harlum says. “A lot of time, effort and expertise has got us to where we’re at.”

title: Jehovah's Getuigen schrappen verbod op bloedtransfusies
content: Jehovah's getuigen mogen voortaan een bloedtransfusie ondergaan. De internationale leiding van de streng religieuze geloofsgemeenschap heeft bekendgemaakt dat het verbod daarop grotendeels wordt geschrapt. Het accepteren van een bloedtransfusie wordt nu een persoonlijke gewetenskwestie voor gelovigen. Zij mogen dus zelf beslissen of ze ermee instemmen. Het verbod blijft alleen gehandhaafd bij zogeheten volbloed-transfusies, waarbij het volledige bloed wordt toegediend. Dit soort transfusies komt echter zelden voor. Bij vrijwel alle bloedtransfusies in Nederland en wereldwijd worden alleen bepaalde delen van het bloed toegediend, zoals rode bloedcellen, plasma of plaatjes. Dat gebeurt bijvoorbeeld bij een hartoperatie, een keizersnede of na een ernstig ongeluk. In het verleden zijn er Jehovah's getuigen overleden nadat ze een bloedtransfusie weigerden. Ook minderjarige patiënten die van hun ouders niet een bloedtransfusie mochten ondergaan overleden na weigering. Veel Jehovah's getuigen die een hartoperatie moeten ondergaan, worden behandeld in het Amphia-ziekenhuis in Breda. Daar zit het Topklinisch Expertisecentrum voor de zorg voor Jehovah's getuigen, het enige van Nederland. Bas Gerritse is cardio-anesthesioloog in het ziekenhuis en coördineert het expertisecentrum. "Dit is een enorme ommekeer van iets wat jaren gespeeld heeft", zegt hij. "Al vele jaren weigeren Jehovah's getuigen bloedtransfusies en plotseling komt het bericht dat dat inzicht in het geloof is herzien." Gerritse verwelkomt het nieuws. "Hartoperaties zijn ingewikkeld en gaan vaak gepaard met veel bloedverlies. Daarom is bloedtransfusie soms nodig." Voor Jehovah's getuigen die dat niet wilden, zijn er in het Amphia-ziekenhuis speciale technieken zodat een operatie zonder bloedtransfusie ook veilig kan verlopen. Nu het verbod vervalt, kunnen zij dus vaker terecht in andere ziekenhuizen. Dat maakt de zorg eenvoudiger en veiliger, zegt de arts. Handelingen 15:20 Dat het hoofdkantoor van de Jehovah's Getuigen het verbod op bloedtransfusie aanpast, heeft te maken met een gesprek dat al langer gaande is in de gemeenschap. Eerder werd het bijvoorbeeld al mogelijk om je eigen bloed met een transfusie toegediend te krijgen. Dat bloed werd dan voor een operatie afgenomen en kon tijdens de operatie worden teruggegeven. Als onderdeel van die discussie heeft het in de Verenigde Staten gevestigde hoofdkantoor ook opnieuw naar de Bijbelpassages gekeken waarop het verbod gebaseerd was. Dat gaat om Handelingen 15:20, waarin staat dat gelovigen geen bloed mogen eten of drinken. Volgens Jehovah's Getuigen valt een bloedtransfusie met volbloed daar dus ook onder. "Decennia hebben we geloofd dat dat ook betrekking had op de vier hoofdelementen van bloed (rode en witte bloedcellen, plaatjes en plasma, red.). Maar omdat de Bijbel het niet specifiek heeft over die componenten, moet iedere Jehovah's getuige beslissen of hij bloed van een ander persoon accepteert", zegt een internationale woordvoerder van het hoofdkantoor in een video op Instagram. De woordvoerder benadrukt daarna ook dat er alternatieven zijn voor bloedtransfusies. Dat soort alternatieve behandelingen worden bijvoorbeeld in het Amphia-ziekenhuis gegeven. "Bij het nemen van de beslissing is vooral het verlangen van Jehovah's getuigen belangrijk om een schoon geweten voor hun God te houden", zegt de woordvoerder. De Nederlandse tak van de gemeenschap zegt in een persbericht de persoonlijke keuzes van geloofsgenoten te zullen blijven "respecteren en steunen". Toen het nieuws gisteren naar buiten kwam, werd Bas Gerritse niet lang daarna gebeld door de coördinator van het Nederlandse hoofdkantoor van de Jehovah's Getuigen. "Hij zei dat hij iets heel belangrijks moest zeggen en was enthousiast om het te vertellen. Zij realiseren zich heel goed dat dit voor veel mensen kan bijdragen aan veiligere zorg."

title: Κωστούλας: Χάρισε τη φανέλα της Μπράιτον σε 8χρονο Έλληνα στο «Ολντ Τράφορντ» (vid)
content:
Ο Μπάμπης Κωστούλας πρωταγωνίστησε μέσα στο γήπεδο και λίγο αργότερα χάρισε μια ξεχωριστή στιγμή σε έναν μικρό Έλληνα φίλαθλο που βρέθηκε στο «Ολντ Τράφορντ».
Ο 8χρονος παρακολούθησε μαζί με τον πατέρα του τη μεγάλη νίκη της Μπράιτον με 3-2 επί της Μάντσεστερ Γιουνάιτεντ, σε μια βραδιά που δύσκολα θα ξεχάσει. Ο Κωστούλας φρόντισε, μάλιστα, να γίνει ακόμη πιο ιδιαίτερη.
Μετά το τελευταίο σφύριγμα, ο Έλληνας επιθετικός πλησίασε τον μικρό φίλαθλο και του χάρισε τη φανέλα της Μπράιτον που φορούσε, προσφέροντάς του ένα αναμνηστικό που θα κρατήσει για πάντα.
Μέσα σε μια βραδιά όπου ο ίδιος είχε καταγράψει ένα γκολ και μία ασίστ, ο Κωστούλας βρήκε τον τρόπο να χαρίσει χαμόγελο και έξω από τον αγωνιστικό χώρο.

title: Ahead of Leh killings anniversary, Ladakh withdraws 20 cases
content:
3 min readSrinagarUpdated: Sep 24, 2026 04:28 AM IST

A year after four civilians were killed in police firing after protests turned violent in Leh, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena on Wednesday announced the withdrawal of criminal cases against 20 of the 87 people booked in the aftermath of that incident. This includes Jigmat Dorjay, Rinchen Dadul, Stanzin Namgail and Tsewang Thirchin, who have died in the past year, as per officials.
Withdrawal of criminal cases has remained one of the key demands of Ladakh’s representatives during ongoing talks with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
This comes a month after the administration stated that it would be filing closure reports for 25 of the 87 people booked in the aftermath of the violence on September 24 last year. Of the 87 identified accused in the rioting cases, 81 were arrested, and criminal proceedings have begun against them.




Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra had earlier said that nine people had been chargesheeted, suggesting that “there is evidence of their involvement” in the incident. He had also stated that LG’s office had directed the Ladakh DGP to “review the cases of the rest of the people who are still part of the investigation”.
On Wednesday, the administration announced the withdrawal of more cases, with LG Saxena stating that the move is “in the larger interest of peace, public tranquillity, and social harmony in Ladakh”.
“Following a comprehensive review, the Ladakh police recommended a closure report for 20 individuals, in FIR no. 144/2005, registered at PS – Leh, under section 360 of the BNSS,” Saxena said in a communique from Lok Niwas.
This decision, he added, ensures that these 20 individuals move forward positively with their lives and careers. “By prioritising justice and healing over protracted litigation, the decision aims at fostering a more peaceful, united, and harmonious society in Ladakh. I extend my sincere gratitude to Hon’ble Union Home Minister, Shri @AmitShah ji for his constant guidance and sympathetic approach, in matters pertaining to the victims and their families.”

This also comes days after the Centre proposed a constitutional provision of ‘Article 371(K)’ in a bid to extend additional protections to Ladakh during a meeting of the sub-committee with the MHA earlier this month. Quashing of the cases has been a key demand of the representatives who have been part of a dialogue with the Centre seeking greater democratic representation and constitutional protections for the region.
The development coincides with a symbolic 20-km march that Ladakh climate activist Sonam Wangchuk will lead to mark the anniversary of the civilian killings in Ladakh.
Four protesters were killed and 44 injured as police fired after a protest for statehood and the Sixth Schedule for Ladakh turned violent in Leh on September 24 last year. After the protests, Wangchuk, who was on a hunger strike at the time of the incident, was booked under the National Security Act (NSA) and lodged in Jodhpur jail for six months.
On September 13, the administration had sanctioned compensation of Rs 15 lakh to the next of kin of each of the four deceased in the September 24 violence. An ex-gratia payment of Rs 3 lakh for those with major injuries and Rs 1 lakh for minor injuries had also been approved.

title: Qatar embassy brings communities together at Ottawa fall gathering
content:
The Embassy of the State of Qatar in Ottawa welcomed members of the Qatari, Canadian and wider local communities to the Ottawa Fall Get-Together at Leamy Lake Park in Gatineau, Quebec, held as part of the 2026 Year of Culture partnership between the two countries.
Bringing together more than 100 attendees, the outdoor gathering celebrated the growing friendship between Qatar and Canada through an afternoon of sport, food and informal cultural exchange. Guests of different ages took part in basketball, volleyball and tug-of-war, creating a relaxed setting in which families and community members could meet and form new connections. Tariq Ali Faraj al-Ansari, ambassador of the State of Qatar to Canada, said: “This gathering represents an exciting manifestation of the cultural exchange between our peoples and sets an example of mutual understanding. The 2026 Year of Culture partnership goes beyond words, as we demonstrate the important nexus between culture, friendship, peace, and development.
“Our message today is that our friendship goes beyond borders, and that our cultural exchange will continue to strengthen and nurture the friendly relations between our two countries and peoples. Together, we can build peaceful and inclusive societies.”
The Qatar, Canada and Mexico 2026 Year of Culture creates opportunities for people to discover one another’s cultures and build lasting relationships. Its programme brings communities, institutions and creative practitioners together through cultural, educational, sporting and community-led activities in the partner countries.
The fall gathering’s strong turnout and warm community atmosphere demonstrated how simple shared experiences can support deeper understanding and lasting people-to-people ties between Qatar and Canada.
The Ottawa Fall Get-Together followed a wide-ranging programme of exchange between Qatar and Canada throughout 2026. In Canada, the Year of Culture was launched with a dedicated media day at the Embassy of Qatar in Ottawa; M7 introduced emerging designers from Qatar to Canadian audiences at Fashion Art Toronto; Qatari artist Ghada al-Suwaidi created a special helmet worn by Pierre Gasly at the Formula 1 Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal; and calligraffiti artist Fatima al-Sharshani produced a public artwork for Montreal’s MURAL Festival. In Toronto, Doha Debates brought together students and voices from sport and media for a Town Hall exploring football fandom, community and commercialisation.
In Qatar, Canadian chefs Christian Gosselin, Eric Chong and Andy Hay shared the country’s diverse culinary traditions at the Qatar International Food Festival, while Canadian artists participated in the inaugural Art Basel Qatar.
Canada’s sporting culture was also celebrated through street curling on National Sport Day and a wider winter sports programme featuring ice hockey, curling and skating, alongside Canadian community participation and cultural activities.
Together, these exchanges have connected artists, designers, chefs, young people, athletes and families, creating new opportunities for Qataris and Canadians to experience one another’s cultures and build lasting relationships.

title: Building a Black Honors Community
content:
California State University, Sacramento
When Naomi Thrower was applying to college, she knew she wanted the historically Black college or university experience but hesitated to leave the community she had built in California, which does not have a traditional HBCU.
So she applied to HBCUs across the country, as well as to California State University, Sacramento, the state’s first Black-serving institution.
“Sacramento State is the only California school I applied to. The rest were all East Coast HBCUs,” Thrower said. “I do have family on the East Coast, but none I felt strongly connected with. So I would be leaving my family, my friends, the life I’ve built here, and that was a little nerve-racking.”
Now a fourth-year deaf studies major, Thrower has found a community in the university’s Black Honors College, a first-of-its-kind program that provides a culturally responsive curriculum and inclusive academic community for students focused on the Black experience.
“It really provided me with a strong social foundation,” said Thrower, who was part of the college's inaugural cohort in 2024. “I knew everybody in my cohort, so when I was in my classes, when we started for the first day, I was nervous, but I already saw familiar faces, and so the [Black Honors College] provided me with that community feel.”
A growing community: Originally announced in 2023, Sacramento State’s Black Honors College offers smaller, specialized general education classes and is open to students of all races and majors. It also provides dedicated mentorship, paid internships, residential living-learning options and scholarships. The model offers a window into what can happen when an honors college centers Black history, culture and experiences in its curriculum while emphasizing community and belonging.
The Black Honors College admits incoming first-year students each fall, while transfer students and continuing Sacramento State sophomores and juniors can apply each spring. Students must have a 3.5 GPA at the time of application and maintain a 3.0 GPA or higher to remain enrolled.
Boatamo Ati Mosupyoe, dean of students and chief academic officer at Sacramento State, said the college initially planned to admit only 50 students in fall 2024, but growing interest led it to admit 80. The fall 2025 class grew to 262 students; this year's class is 414 students, bringing the total enrollment to 914.
Mosupyoe attributes that growth in part to the environment the college has sought to create, one that emphasizes students’ strengths rather than approaching them from what she described as a deficit perspective.
“We are creating a welcoming environment to the students,” Mosupyoe said. “This program doesn’t look at the students as deficient, and we don’t subscribe to a deficit model. We look at the potential of what these students are going to do.”
Matthew Ward, vice president of strategic enrollment management and chief enrollment officer, said the Black Honors College has become part of a broader effort at the university to intentionally support Black students and celebrate Black culture.
“We have lots of students who think about HBCUs but have to consider traveling across the country to go to an institution where they’re going to find that Black joy, Black excellence, Black dignity,” Ward said. “From what I’ve seen, in terms of the broader growth … word travels fast. There is definitely among students and families and school districts and educational leaders a real focus on Sacramento because it’s doing something that’s against the grain.”
That sense of community appealed to Manuel Tellez, a transfer student who grew up in Sacramento’s Oak Park neighborhood. Entering Sacramento State as a first-generation student, Tellez said he knew he needed the guidance of a strong Black community to feel comfortable and push himself academically, which he found in the Black Honors College.
“The Black Honors College pushed me to the next level [and] held me to a higher standard,” Tellez said. “Ever since then, my GPA has climbed, and I’ve been comfortable with going to school.”
Leland O’Neal, assistant program coordinator for the Black Honors College, said another strength of the college is the range of students and experiences represented within its cohorts.
“The pace of expansion has surprised me a little bit, but in a grand way,” O’Neal said. “We have students in that cohort, like Manuel, who are transfer students, but we also have students coming in who are as old as 69 or students who are as young as 19. So I think you really get a diverse array of perspectives and experiences.”
Building a network: As the Black Honors College has grown, so have its student supports. The college now offers financial literacy workshops, access to an in-house licensed therapist and events that celebrate Black culture. Mosupyoe said the number of professors affiliated with the college has also grown from 20 when the college began to 30 today.
“We have a community of administrators, staff and professors who are helping us really make sure that we provide what we have promised to students,” Mosupyoe said.
For Thrower, that support has extended beyond the classroom. She now works as a student assistant for the college and in that capacity has helped organize programming with the nonprofit Black Deaf Project to connect and socialize with students. The experience ultimately led her to an internship with the organization.
“The first piece of advice I got before college was that your net worth is your network,” Thrower said. “The Black Honors College has been that foundational network hub. I know people all over campus, and if I don’t know where to find some information, I know that I can go to the Black Honors College and they can direct me towards somebody who can help.”

title: Enable Through Dance: breaking barriers for dancers with disabilities
content:
Enable Through Dance: breaking barriers for dancers with disabilities
“It’s about giving young people living with disabilities a chance to explore potential that they have not before”
To mark ten years of the Enable Through Dance programme, learners with disabilities took centre stage with professional dancers from the Moving Into Dance non-profit company at the Keorapetse William Kgositsile Theatre at the University of Johannesburg Arts Centre on the weekend.
The programme, established in 2016, works with over 160 learners from several schools and organisations across Johannesburg. They use dance and movement to give young people with disabilities opportunities for creative expression, while building their confidence and self-esteem.
Moving Into Dance, based in Newtown, was established in 1978 by Sylvia Glasser. As one of only a few mixed-race dance groups at the time, it used dance as cultural resistance against the apartheid regime.
The anniversary performance at the weekend was open to the public free of charge.
Nadia Virasamy, CEO of Moving Into Dance, said the programme started with the organisation having to reconsider its own understanding of dance and disability.
Virasamy said this was challenging for a professional dance company whose work had traditionally focused on particular ideas of physical ability and movement.
“It isn’t about ability or disability, it’s about inclusivity,” she said. “It’s about giving young people living with disabilities a chance to explore this potential that they have not before.”
Moving Into Dance brings in specialists to work with the dancers and facilitators. The programme eventually became a weekly initiative in schools and organisations around Johannesburg.
The project offers more than simply teaching dance techniques, said Virasamy. She has seen young people become more confident and comfortable when interacting with people.
“There’s no demarcation about who can do what within the space,” she said. “It’s everybody together embracing this beautiful art form we call dance.”
One of the dancers, 29-year-old Tebogo Lelaletse, is from the North West and uses a wheelchair. He started dancing in 2019 with Unmute Cape Town before joining the Moving Into Dance company.
He said dance has given him a way to tell stories and express emotions without having to rely on speech.
“Sometimes I feel like when I’m speaking, everybody’s muting you,” he said. “So, it’s better if you talk through movement.”
Lelaletse also encouraged other people with disabilities to explore their talents in spite of their fears.
“Whatever gift we have, let’s use it,” he said.
Professional dancer Lesego Dihemo, who teaches learners at Johannesburg School for Autism, said she initially struggled because she had no experience of working with autistic learners.
Dihemo was trained through the Enable Through Dance programme and also did her own research about autism and seeking advice from teachers at the school.
She said the experience changed her as both a teacher and a dancer.
“When you are with the kids, you find the love, the laughter, you become free,” she said. “Your creativity just opens up with them.”
She said she has also developed a better understanding of what inclusive practice really means.

title: WATCH: Nursing licensure exam passers, loved ones cry tears of joy after learning results
content:
WATCH: Nursing licensure exam passers, loved ones cry tears of joy after learning results
Students who passed the recent nursing exams were able to have sweet moments with their families as they celebrated their achievements.
According to a report on "24 Oras," Youscooper Heaven waited for the results with her family and subsequently yelled with joy with them after seeing that she passed.
Meanwhile, Youscooper Francis celebrated with his grandmother, who then had lechon prepared for his achievement.
Then there was Youscooper Valrexie, who was in tears as she shared the results with her migrant worker brother.
Valrexie and her brother no longer have parents, so the latter had to work for the former’s studies.
The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) said that 28,652 out of 37,359 takers were able to pass. –Jean Mangaluz/NB, GMA News

title: Harminc perccel csökkent a házimunka nők és férfiak közötti különbsége. Mitől?
content:
Harminc perccel csökkent a házimunka nők és férfiak közötti különbsége. Mitől?
A szerző területfejlesztési közgazdász, fejlesztési szakember, auditor.
Tizenöt év alatt napi fél órával csökkent Magyarországon a nők és a férfiak háztartási munkára fordított ideje közötti különbség. Első ránézésre ez elég egyértelmű javulásnak tűnik.
A KSH 2009-2010-es időmérleg-felvétele szerint a 15-74 éves nők naponta átlagosan 183 percet töltöttek háztartási és ház körüli munkával, a férfiak 78-at. A 2024-2025-ös felvétel előzetes adatai szerint ez 174, illetve 99 perc. A különbség 105 percről 75-re csökkent.
Ez érdemi változás, a napi 30 perces közeledés éves szinten több mint 180 órát jelent. Közben viszont egy jelenleg zajló, nem reprezentatív adatfelvételemben, amelyben magyar nőket kérdezek a családi munkamegosztásról és a mentális terhelésről, továbbra is visszatérően előkerül a háztartás működtetésének terhe. Nemcsak a mosásról, főzésről vagy takarításról írnak, hanem arról is, hogy valakinek folyamatosan szerveznie, figyelnie és észben tartania kell.
A kétféle adat nem mond ellent egymásnak. Együtt viszont felvetnek egy kérdést: ha a nők és a férfiak házimunkára fordított ideje ennyit közeledett, miért jelenik meg a női beszámolókban továbbra is ennyire erősen az otthoni teher, a szervezés és az állandó észben tartás?*
A válasz első része már a KSH részletes adataiból is látszik. A 30 perces közeledés nem egyszerűen úgy alakult ki, hogy a férfiak átvették a nők korábbi feladatait.
Nem ugyanott nőtt, ahol csökkent
Ha egyszerű feladatátadás történt volna, azt várnánk, hogy ahol a nőknél csökken az időráfordítás, ott a férfiaknál nő. Van, ahol valóban ez történt. A férfiak főzésre, terítésre és tálalásra 2009-2010-ben átlagosan napi 18 percet fordítottak, 2024-2025-ben már 27-et. Lakástakarításra és rendrakásra napi 8 helyett 16 percet szánnak.
Csakhogy a nőknél nem ezeknél a munkáknál tűntek el a percek. A főzésre fordított idejük 79 perc volt tizenöt éve, és ugyanennyi most is. Takarítással pedig nem kevesebbet, hanem többet foglalkoznak, napi 33 helyett 38 percet.
A nagy változás máshol történt. A nők mosogatásra fordított napi ideje 33 percről 13-ra, a mosásra és vasalásra jutó idő 21-ről 12 percre esett. A férfiaknál közben a mosogatás ideje nem nőtt, hanem 6 percről 3-ra csökkent, mosásra és vasalásra pedig 1 helyett 2 percet fordítanak.
Ezek alapján legalább két folyamat látszik egymás mellett. A férfiak bizonyos rendszeresen végzett háztartási feladatokban ténylegesen aktívabbak lettek, miközben néhány, korábban különösen sok női időt elvivő munka időigénye jelentősen csökkent.
A nők házimunkájából eltűnt perceket tehát nem egyszerűen a férfiak dolgozzák le helyettük.
A mosogatás és a mosás időigényének csökkenésében technológiai, szolgáltatási vagy más életmódbeli változások is szerepet játszhattak.*
Érdemes azt is megnézni, mi történt eközben a háztartási munka teljes mennyiségével. A 15-74 éves lakosság napi átlaga 2009-2010-ben 133 perc volt, 2024-2025-ben 137. Vagyis nem arról van szó, hogy egyszerűen sokkal kevesebb háztartási munkát végzünk.
Közben a fizetett munkára fordított idő is nőtt
Az időfelhasználás egy másik nagy szelete is megváltozott. A nők főfoglalkozásra fordított napi átlagos ideje 123 percről 170-re emelkedett, a férfiaké 183-ról 234-re.*
A háztartási munka átalakulása tehát nem változatlan időfelhasználási környezetben történt.*
A közeledés mindenesetre nem most kezdődött. A KSH négy időmérleg-felvételében minden alkalommal kisebb volt a nemek közötti különbség, mint az előző mérésben. 1986-1987-ben a nők napi 208, a férfiak 62 percet fordítottak háztartási és ház körüli munkára, vagyis 146 perc volt a rés. 1999-2000-ben 121 perc, 2009-2010-ben 105, 2024-2025-ben pedig 75.
A mostani napi 75 perc azért továbbra is heti 8 óra 45 perc különbséget jelent.
A hosszú idősorból tehát elég biztosan látszik, hogy a nők és férfiak által elvégzett háztartási munka időigénye közeledett. Azt ebből még nem tudjuk, hogy ugyanilyen mértékben változott-e az is, ki felel azért, hogy a háztartás működjön.
Nem ugyanaz elvégezni és fejben tartani
Az időmérleg egyik nagy előnye, hogy nem arra kérdez rá, ki érzi úgy, hogy sok házimunkát végez, hanem konkrét tevékenységeket rögzít. A főzést könnyű időben elhelyezni, ahogy a takarítást, a mosogatást vagy a bevásárlást is.
Nehezebb ugyanezt megtenni azzal, hogy valaki észrevette, elfogyott a tej. Fejben tartotta, mikor lesz szülői értekezlet. Végignézte, hol lehet időpontot kapni a gyereknek fogorvoshoz, egyeztetett, megszervezte, ki viszi el, majd emlékezett arra is, mire lesz még szükség.
Ezek ráadásul gyakran nem elkülönülő időblokkok. A bevásárlólista összeállhat munka közben, egy időpont megszervezése pedig több rövid keresésből, telefonból és egyeztetésből. Emiatt nehezebb ugyanúgy percekre bontani őket, mint a főzést.
A szakirodalom ezt kognitív háztartási munkaként különíti el a fizikai végrehajtástól. A kérdés nemcsak az, hogy egyenlőtlenül oszlik-e meg, hanem az is, hogy van-e mérhető kapcsolata a kimerültséggel.
Andreas Haupt és Dafna Gelbgiser tíz európai ország országosan reprezentatív mintáiból származó adatokat elemeztek. A végső elemzésben Bulgária, Oroszország, Georgia, Franciaország, Románia, Belgium, Litvánia, Lengyelország, Csehország és Svédország szerepelt. A vizsgálatban foglalkoztatott, heteroszexuális párkapcsolatban élő válaszadóknál nézték a kognitív háztartási munka megosztását és azt, hogy a háztartási munka miatti kimerültség mennyire nyúlik át a fizetett munkába.
A nőknél az egyenlően megosztott kognitív munka mellett 9 százalékra becsülték annak valószínűségét, hogy valaki havonta többször túl fáradtan érkezik a munkahelyére a háztartási munka miatt ahhoz, hogy megfelelően teljesítsen. Ha a nő valamennyi vizsgált kognitív feladatot maga végezte, ez 15 százalék volt. Ha a partner végezte az összeset, 6 százalék. A férfiaknál nem találtak ugyanilyen összefüggést.*
Egy másik vizsgálatban Elizabeth Aviv és munkatársai 322 kisgyermekes anyát kérdeztek ugyanazon 30 háztartási feladatról, külön a tervezésről és a fizikai végrehajtásról. A résztvevők saját beszámolóik szerint átlagosan a kognitív háztartási munka 72,57 százalékáért, a fizikai végrehajtás 63,64 százalékáért voltak felelősek. A nagyobb kognitív rész ebben a mintában több depressziós tünettel, magasabb stresszel és személyes kiégéssel, rosszabb általános mentális állapottal és gyengébb párkapcsolati működéssel járt együtt.
A vizsgálat jól megmutatja, hogy ugyanazon feladatokon belül a tervezés és a fizikai végrehajtás felelőssége nem feltétlenül ugyanúgy oszlik meg.*
A hazai válaszokban is megjelenik ez a különbség
A most futó online adatfelvételemben külön kérdezek rá arra, hogy a család működtetéséhez szükséges tervezés, szervezés és észben tartás mekkora része jut a válaszadóra. Arra is, ki veszi észre az elintézendő dolgokat, ki tartja fejben a határidőket és időpontokat, ki szervezi a gyermekekkel kapcsolatos ügyeket, és előfordul-e, hogy a válaszadó akkor is követi a feladatot, amikor végül más végzi el.
Az adatfelvétel még folyamatban van, az eddigi válaszok pedig abból a szempontból érdekesek, hogy megmutatják, mit neveznek meg maguktól a válaszadók, amikor azt kérdezem tőlük, miben fáradtak el mostanában úgy, hogy ezt mások alig vagy egyáltalán nem veszik észre.*
Volt, aki mindössze annyit írt: „minden megszervezése.” Másnak a „folyamatos figyelés mindenkire” jelent terhet. Egy válaszadó az otthoni láthatatlan munka, a gyerekek körüli ügyek és a saját munka összeegyeztetését emelte ki. Egy két kamaszt nevelő anya pedig azt írta, hogy „sokszor csak akkor veszik észre a házimunkát (mosás, tiszta ruha, ételkészítés), ha az valamiért elmarad.”
Ezek a mondatok jól mutatják, miért lehet fontos különválasztani a konkrét feladat elvégzését attól, hogy valaki észreveszi, előre gondolkodik, szervez, összehangol és követ.*
Ennek a kimerültség kezelésénél is van jelentősége. A relaxáció, a meditáció, a tudatos légzés és más stresszkezelési eszközök segíthetik a regenerációt, de nem változtatják meg önmagukban a terhelést létrehozó körülményeket. Ha például a folyamatos szervezési felelősség tartósan egy embernél marad, annak következményeit nem lehet kizárólag az ő stresszkezelési feladataként kezelni.
Akkor mitől lett kisebb a különbség?
A 105 percről 75-re csökkenő résre nincs egyetlen válasz. A férfiak valóban több időt fordítanak néhány rendszeres háztartási tevékenységre, különösen a főzésre és a takarításra. A nőknél viszont az időráfordítás legnagyobb csökkenése más feladatoknál, például a mosogatásnál, illetve a mosásnál és vasalásnál történt. Ezeknél nem látunk hasonló nagyságú, ellenkező irányú változást a férfiaknál.
Közben mindkét nemnél nőtt a főfoglalkozásra fordított átlagos idő, és technológiai, fogyasztási vagy más társadalmi változások is alakíthatták azt, hogyan végezzük a háztartási munkát.*
Mindezek miatt a 30 perces csökkenést túl egyszerű lenne úgy összefoglalni, hogy a férfiak átvették a nők házimunkájának egy részét.
A konkrét háztartási munkára fordított időben valóban közeledtek egymáshoz a nők és a férfiak, azt viszont ebből nem tudjuk, hogy ugyanilyen mértékben újraosztódott-e a háztartás és a család működtetésének felelőssége is. Erre Magyarországon egyelőre nincs az időmérleghez hasonló minőségű adatunk. Azt már elég pontosan meg tudjuk mondani, ki vásárolt be. Azt jóval kevésbé, hogy ki tudta, aznap mit kell megvenni, és hol.

title: Burkina/Entrepreneuriat : Yamdicré Academy forme une trentaine de jeunes en saponification
content:
Burkina/Entrepreneuriat : Yamdicré Academy forme une trentaine de jeunes en saponification
Ouagadougou, 19 septembre 2026 (AIB)-La structure Yamdicré Academy a organisé, du 18 au 19 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une formation gratuite en saponification au profit d’une trentaine de jeunes, sous le thème « Formation, jeunesse et entrepreneuriat ».
« L’initiative vise à permettre au jeune d’acquérir des compétences pratiques dans différents métiers », a déclaré le promoteur de Yamdicré Academy, par ailleurs formateur, Wendkuni Barnabas Ouédraogo.
Selon lui, « cette initiative s’inscrit dans une démarche de conscientisation de la jeunesse et de promotion de l’entrepreneuriat ».
« Durant les deux jours de formation, les participants ont appris la fabrication du savon de lessive, du savon liquide, du kabakourou, de l’eau de Javel, du shampooing », a affirmé Wendkuni Barnabas Ouédraogo.
« La fabrication de la pommade de beauté, la pommade mentholée et également des conseils pour être utile à la société », a-t-il ajouté.
M. Ouédraogo a exhorté les bénéficiaires à mettre en pratique les connaissances acquises. « Nous sommes les dignes fils de ce pays et nous avons le devoir de nous sacrifier pour la génération future ».
Pour sa part, la bénéficiaire Asséta Konkobo a salué l’initiative portée par la structure Yamdicré Academy.
Elle a laissé entendre que « grâce à cette formation, j’aurai désormais une source de revenus à travers la production du savon liquide ».
De son côté, Fatoumata Ouédraogo s’est engagée à partager les connaissances acquises au cours de la formation afin d’en faire bénéficier sa communauté.
Née en janvier 2025, Yamdicré Academy œuvre pour la formation de la jeunesse, la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat et le développement personnel.
